role.title: Director of Operations-Life Sciences
role.description:
**Who we are:**

Charter Medical, part of the Solesis family of companies, specializes in single-use solutions that enable life sciences innovators to turn bold ideas into lasting breakthroughs, supporting industry-leading companies in bringing life-saving therapies to market. Operating in North Carolina, Charter Medical employs more than 150 team members across two facilities in Winston-Salem.

Guided by a commitment to quality, innovation and customer success, Charter partners with customers to transform promising therapies into commercial realities. Employees contribute to solutions that support life-changing treatments and make a meaningful impact on patients around the world.

**1st shift Monday-Friday 8:00 am-5:00 pm**

**About the role:**

The Director of Operations provides strategic and operational leadership for the site, with full accountability for Profit & Loss (P&L) performance, manufacturing excellence, and sustainable, profitable growth in single-use cell processing and biopharmaceutical manufacturing. The role translates Charter Medical’s mission into operating priorities that advance purpose-built, customizable processing solutions, reduce the cost and risk of delivering advanced therapies, and enable customers to scale reliably. By aligning capacity, capital investment, innovation, quality, and workforce capability with customer demand, the Director fosters a culture of safety, compliance, responsiveness, collaboration, urgency, and continuous improvement—helping biopharmaceutical innovators make life-changing therapies more accessible to patients.

**What you will do:**

* Lead all site manufacturing operations to ensure safe, compliant, reliable, and profitable execution of customer demand.
* Own site P&L performance, including revenue attainment, EBITDA, gross margin, labor and overhead management, productivity, spending, savings, and budget execution.
* Develop and execute the site operating plan and manufacturing strategy in alignment with company objectives, customer demand, and growth priorities.
* Direct manufacturing execution, facilities, maintenance, and continuous improvement activities to achieve Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People objectives.
* Ensure effective utilization of labor, equipment, materials, information, and facility capacity to improve throughput, yield, lead time, asset utilization, and on-time delivery.
* Establish, review, and act on key performance indicators and performance trends through daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual operating reviews.
* Evaluate and improve manufacturing methods using knowledge of product requirements, materials, fabrication processes, tooling, equipment capability, work methods, and quality-control standards.
* Lead capacity planning and resource allocation to support current production, new business, customer growth, and future site requirements.
* Develop, justify, prioritize, and execute capital investment plans supporting safety, compliance, capacity, automation, productivity, business continuity, and site growth.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, delivery, yield, scrap, labor productivity, cost reduction, flow, and equipment reliability.
* Ensure product availability through disciplined execution of the production plan and alignment of labor, materials, equipment, and technical support.
* Support new-product introductions, technology transfers, pilot builds, process scale-up, design-for-manufacturability reviews, product validations, and commercialization activities.
* Partner with Commercial and Product Development teams to assess manufacturing capability, support customer opportunities, align operational commitments, and respond to changing demand.
* Serve as the senior manufacturing representative during customer visits, business reviews, audits, regulatory inspections, CAPA activities, and issue-resolution efforts.
* Ensure manufacturing execution meets product specifications, documentation, and traceability requirements and supports compliant delivery.
* Build and maintain robust manufacturing training and qualification programs in partnership with Human Resources.
* Develop annual operating budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, productivity targets, and capital plans; monitor performance and implement corrective actions when results fall below plan.
* Oversee product-costing inputs based on actual manufacturing performance, labor productivity, yields, scrap, material usage, and operational assumptions in partnership with Finance.
* Identify staffing requirements; participate in selection and hiring; build organizational capability to meet operational and growth requirements.
* Coach, mentor, and develop operations leaders and employees; establish clear expectations, provide ongoing feedback, manage performance, and support succession and career development.
* Partner with Human Resources to maintain an effective organization structure, conduct talent reviews, improve employee engagement, and develop leadership capability.
* Foster a culture of safety, accountability, quality, customer focus, collaboration, disciplined execution, and continuous improvement throughout the site.
* Ensure adherence to site safety requirements, PPE practices, environmental expectations, and applicable Health, Safety, and Environmental systems.
* Maintain strong communication across shifts, departments, and leadership so priorities, risks, decisions, and customer commitments are clearly understood.
* Act independently with a high degree of judgment and initiative to resolve complex manufacturing and business issues and develop recommendations for senior leadership.

***Please note that Charter Medical does not provide employment visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship both now or in the future.***

**Who you are:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, life sciences, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including significant experience in a regulated life sciences, biopharmaceutical, medical device, or comparable environment.
* Minimum of 4 years of experience in manufacturing management, plant leadership, or director-level role.
* Demonstrated experience owning or significantly influencing a manufacturing P&L, operating budget, productivity plan, and capital portfolio.
* Demonstrated ability to lead managers and cross-functional teams, coach employees, resolve conflict, and drive accountability.
* Working knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices, FDA expectations, ISO-based quality systems, and regulated manufacturing documentation.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, equipment capability, facilities, maintenance, cost drivers, and operational workflows.
* Considerable knowledge of ERP systems and proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.
* Effective written, verbal, presentation, analytical, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work across shared-service and matrixed organizations.
* Ability to use Lean Six Sigma and structured problem-solving methods to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and business performance.
* Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.
* Experience in cleanroom manufacturing preferred.
* Experience supporting biopharmaceutical customers, customer audits, and contract manufacturing operations preferred.
* Experience leading capacity expansion, automation, technology transfer, or operational transformation initiatives preferred.

**Perks / Benefits:**

* Generous Paid Time Off
* Paid Breaks
* Annual Bonus
* 401(k) with excellent company match
* Health Insurance with multiple plans to choose from
* Paid Short Term and Long Term Disability

Equal Opportunity Employer 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

role.description:
**Title:** **Sr Manager, GCP Quality Assurance**
================================================

Date: Oct 29, 2026

Location: Princeton, NJ

Company: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc (USA)

The Sr Manager, GCP Quality Assurance (Asset Lead) provides strategic quality oversight for assigned development programs within the Sun Pharma Global Development Organization (GDO) Branded Portfolio within Innovative Medicines. The role serves as the primary Quality asset representative to cross-functional global project teams and ensures compliance with applicable GXP regulations, company quality standards, and risk-based quality management principles across the clinical development lifecycle.

 

Key Responsibilities:

* Serve as the primary Quality representative for assigned assets/programs.
* Provide quality risk assessments and strategic recommendations to asset teams.
* Represents QA on the clinical and non-clinical teams; Quality Assurance oversight ensures compliance to regulations, guidance, local laws, and applicable ISO standards, TORO, approved protocol, study plans, risk management, safety and product quality reporting requirements and use of validated systems for patient safety, investigational product quality, and data integrity.
* Plans, conducts, and reports GCP audits of clinical trial sites, CROs, vendors, laboratories, internal processes, computerized systems, and regulatory submission documentation in accordance with applicable regulations and procedures.
* Ensures that the GCP Audit schedules are created and approved by QA management; create and execute audit plans that ensure compliance to applicable regulations, guidance/ guidelines, and standard operating procedures.
* Able to travel to conduct audits onsite at vendors’ facilities, service providers, clinical trial sites, and/or internal Sun systems. Proficient to read/write/review written regulatory submission documents to ensure the content is compliant to regulatory requirements. Performs For-cause/Directed Audits when assigned.
* Supports/ Leads company inspection readiness preparations and hosts inspector onsite and via remote tools; Serves as Sponsor QA to support Clinical Site inspections, as required
* Influence clinical development decisions through quality expertise. Assess quality implications of protocol amendments, study design changes, vendor strategies, and regulatory commitments. Collaborate with Outsourcing, Non-clinical, Clinical teams and functional departments (including clinical supplies and project managers) to support the selection of vendors and service providers based on risk evaluation thru audit; manage complex organizational issues, identify and implement organizational mitigations and/or process improvements.
* Escalate significant quality risks to senior leadership. Monitors quality metrics, audit observations, CAPAs, deviations, and critical quality events to identify emerging trends and risks. Provides regular reporting to senior management and develops proactive mitigation strategies in collaboration with functional stakeholders.
* Support the implementation of procedures and quality systems used to support the GDO Sponsored trials and for audit conduct of vendors, labs, clinical trial sites, and submissions dossiers.
* Travel requirement is 20% domestic and international

Requirements:

* BS Degree in Chemistry, Biology, or related scientific discipline; advanced degree preferred. A minimum of 10 years of experience in clinical research, clinical quality assurance, or GxP-regulated environments within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, or clinical research organizations.
* Demonstrated expertise in ICH-GCP, FDA, EMA, ISO and global regulatory requirements.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and inspection readiness programs.
* Experience providing quality oversight to Phase I-IV clinical development programs.
* Strong risk-based quality management and stakeholder influencing skills; ability to communicate with technical and non-technical colleagues; experience establishing and maintaining effective relationships with leaders and peers.

* Demonstrated capability as organizational change agent. Ability to lead and participate on teams with shared responsibility for outcomes and decision-making.

The presently-anticipated base compensation pay range for this position is $150,500 to $183,500. Actual base compensation may vary based on a number of factors, including but not limited to geographical location and experience. In addition, this position is part of the Annual Performance Bonus Plan. Employees are eligible to participate in Company employee benefit programs which include medical, dental and vision coverage; life insurance; disability insurance; 401(k) savings plan; flexible spending accounts; and the employee assistance program. Employees also receive various paid time off benefits, including vacation time and sick time.

 

The compensation and benefits described above are subject to the terms and conditions of any governing plans, policies, practices, agreements, or other materials or documents as in effect from time to time, including but not limited to terms and conditions regarding eligibility. If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company, or individual department/team performance, and market factors.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Why We Stand Out**

Seeking a career-defining opportunity where your leadership, strategic vision, and client expertise are recognized and rewarded? Kaufman Rossin might be just the place for you.

As one of the top accounting firms in the country, our foundation is “people first.” In the words of James Kaufman, “we prioritize our people, their development, and their well-being. Our values are translated into action every day.”

Kaufman Rossin is a privately owned, independent public accounting firm, which means we are not beholden to outside investors or private equity influence. This independence allows us to prioritize long-term client relationships, maintain objectivity in our advisory approach, and make strategic decisions that benefit our people and clients, not external stakeholders. Our structure fosters agility, entrepreneurial thinking, and a collaborative culture where leadership is accessible, and innovation is encouraged.

Celebrated as the Best Place to Work in South Florida over a dozen times, Kaufman Rossin has grown to over 700 employees, with offices spanning the tri-county area, including sister entities Kaufman Rossin Wealth and Kaufman Rossin Alternative Investment Services.

**Think you have what it takes?**

**How You'll Contribute**

Kaufman Rossin is seeking a **Director of Operations** to lead firm-wide initiatives, strengthen operational practices, and turn strategy into execution. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and partnering closely with the Chief Information Officer and firm leadership, you’ll lead our project managers and business analysts while driving technology implementations, process improvements, and organizational change.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys understanding how the business works, staying close to the details, and improving the experience of our clients and colleagues.

* Lead and develop project managers and business analysts, setting priorities, removing roadblocks, and ensuring consistent, high-quality delivery.
* Oversee multiple firm-wide initiatives, balancing scope, timelines, resources, and business impact while staying actively involved in requirements, planning, testing, and rollout.
* Lead the operational side of technology implementations, from selection and requirements through deployment, adoption, and ongoing optimization, in partnership with the CIO and IT team.
* Drive change management through communication, training, and adoption planning, recognizing how people and culture influence success.
* Develop and maintain policies, procedures, and best practices, and implement process improvements across departments.
* Establish business plans, key performance indicators, and performance targets; monitor results through reporting, audits, and scorecards.
* Ensure compliance with professional standards, regulatory requirements, and internal quality programs while identifying and addressing operational risks.
* Oversee team hiring, staffing, training, performance discussions, and career development, fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Manage budgets, forecasts, and the financial performance of operational initiatives, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and profitability.
* Partner with the COO and firm leadership on strategic and growth initiatives that enhance the client and colleague experience.

 
**Requirements**

**How You'll Contribute**

* 7+ years of related operations, project, or program management experience.

* 10+ years of supervisory leadership experience, ideally managing project managers, business analysts, or similar teams.
* Demonstrated success leading technology implementations and organizational change, with a strong understanding of the process from requirements through adoption.
* A hands-on leadership style, strong emotional intelligence, and the ability to manage multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong analytical, organizational, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, supported by sound judgment.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with partners, executives, and staff.
* Proficiency with project management and operational reporting tools.
* Availability for occasional travel to support leadership alignment, training, and firm-wide initiatives.

**How You'll Stand Out**

* Experience in professional services, particularly accounting, finance, risk management, or consulting.
* Bachelor’s degree.
* PMP, Prosci, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certifications.
* Experience with Microsoft Office, Salesforce, Domo, Power BI, or generative AI tools.

 
**Benefits**

***We embrace authenticity.*** *Kaufman Rossin is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating a culture that reflects the diversity of our firm and clients. We encourage understanding, acceptance, and celebration among all people. role.description:
Job Title: Head of Operations
 Employment Status: Full-time
 Office Hours: Monday - Friday; 4:1 hybrid schedule
 Location: Boston, Massachusetts
 Compensation: $175,000-200,000 base + variable + equity options
*compensation may be negotiated based on experience level

 About Ketryx: 

 Ketryx is an AI platform that enables healthcare and life sciences companies to ship life-saving products in weeks instead of years.

 Exploding product complexity is burying companies in compliance paperwork and blocking innovation. Our AI software removes this friction, dissolving the historical tradeoff between innovation and compliance, and enables regulated industries to innovate at the pace of modern software.

 Ketryx already touches the lives of millions of patients and powers 4 of the world’s top 5 life science companies and 25% of the Fortune 500 life science market. Backed by Lightspeed Ventures, our founders are the former Head of AI at Amgen and CTO of Wolfram Cloud.

 Healthcare and life sciences is just the beginning for us. Automotive, aerospace, energy — if it’s regulated, it’s because society decided it matters. These products move humanity, shape our future, and are safety-critical. Come join us and help build the AI platform to power safe innovation.

 The Role 

 We're hiring a Head of Operations to own all things operations & people as Ketryx scales. You'll inherit a small, capable team and a company that is growing quickly across the US and Europe, with all the ambiguity and opportunity that comes with it. Your mandate is over the people here at Ketryx & how we work, by building + refining our systems, hiring engine, and culture that allow us to grow fast and execute without losing what makes our team effective.

 This is a hands-on leadership role based in Boston, including quarterly travel to our Vienna office. You'll set our strategy around cross-functional collaboration, be responsible for designing how we work, and answer a tactical People question in Slack. Our customers build products that keep people alive. The faster we help them ship safely, the sooner these products reach patients. How well we hire, develop, and support our own team is critical!

 You will report to Erez, our CEO and Co-founder

 Responsibilities 

 Business operations 

 
 Build and run the operating system. Design Ketryx's operating rhythm end to end: weekly leadership meetings, monthly business reviews, quarterly planning and retros, and annual goal setting. Make it one cadence across Boston and Vienna.

 Own planning and OKRs. Lead the annual and multi-year operating plan with Erez and Finance. Run the company-wide OKR process, from setting goals to grading them.

 Define and track company KPIs. Set the metrics that tell us whether we're winning across GTM, Product, Engineering, and Delivery. Build a single source of truth for them, and use AI tools to automate the reporting instead of assembling it by hand.

 Drive cross-functional initiatives. Take the company's highest-priority projects that span teams, resolve ownership gaps, and see them through. Lead root-cause analysis when something critical breaks.

 Build for the next stage. Spot where our processes, tools, and structures won't hold as we grow, and fix them before they break. Over time, hire and lead a small business operations team.

 
 People & talent strategy 

 
 Lead the Talent and People leaders. Manage our (Director/Manager) of Talent Acquisition and (Director/Manager) of People. They own day-to-day execution in their departments; you set direction, coach them, and hold their teams to annual goals and metrics tied to company OKRs.

 Set the people strategy. Translate the company plan into a people plan: where we invest in headcount, which capabilities we build or buy, and how the org should be structured as we scale.

 
 Required Skills 

 
 8+ years in HR/People Operations with at least three leading the function or a major pillar of it, especially at high growth startups

 Strong opinions on what can work, a willingness to try something new, and a network of People leaders to tap into for broader questions

 Direct experience scaling a company through significant headcount growth — you've seen what breaks at 100, 200, 500 people and have opinions about it

 Comfort operating without a large team or established playbook — you build the thing and then run it

 Strong recruiting instincts; you can assess engineering and GTM talent markets and partner credibly with engineering leaders

 Demonstrated ownership of compensation and leveling design

 Multi-country employment experience (US and EU) or clear evidence you can get up to speed fast

 Sound judgment in ambiguous, confidential situations, and the directness to bring hard news to the leadership team early

 
 Preferred Skills 

 
 Experience supporting distributed teams across US and European time zones

 Competitive compensation

 Generous stock options possible

 Work in an exciting field with a positive impact on the world

 Opportunity to learn and grow as part of a global team

 Generous PTO for full-time
